newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Rwanda tribunal detains ex-journalist for 30 days.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda tribunal detains ex-journalist for 30 days.

text.p: The U.N.'s Rwanda genocide tribunal on Tuesday extended for 30 days the detention of a former newspaper editor, court officials said.

Presiding Judge Laity Kama of Senegal ordered Rwandan Hassan Ngeze, editor of the radical Hutu Kangura newspaper, detained for a further 30 days to allow the prosecution time to gather evidence and prepare a more precise indictment.
Kenya police working with officials from the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR) last month arrested Ngeze and seven other suspects in Nairobi.
They included Jean Kambanda, prime minister during the 1994 genocide, and Belgian former journalist Georges Ruggiu. Two of the eight suspects were indicted.
Ngeze, already detained for 30 days, appeared in court on Monday but refused to answer questions from the prosecution about an affidavit he had made.

Ngeze's lawyers opposed the extension, arguing he wanted to clear his name and was unlikely to disappear if released. The prosecution said Ngeze was found with several passports and was well connected.
The tribunal based at Arusha, north Tanzania, extended for 30 days on Monday the detention of four suspects including Ruggiu. Kambanda's detention was extended last Thursday for 30 days.
The ICTR was set up in November 1994 to bring to justice leaders of the genocide in which an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and some moderate Hutus were killed.
Twenty-three suspects have been indicted and the tribunal holds 20 in custody in Arusha. Three trials are in progress.
